newsitem.title: INDIA: Thousands detained after India politician arrested.
newsitem.headline: Thousands detained after India politician arrested.

text.p: More than 5,000 people were detained after the arrest of India's best-known woman politician in a corruption case, and one protester died after setting himself on fire, news agencies said on Sunday.

Some 400 supporters of Jayaram Jayalalitha, former chief minister of Tamil Nadu state, were held in the northern Arcot-Ambedkar district for stoning and damaging state buses, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
Thousands more activists from Jayalalitha's All India Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) party were detained amid scattered incidents elsewhere in the state, it said.

Three buses were set on fire and 75 others were damaged, the news agency said. Fourteen Jayalalitha supporters were detained in Madras when they tried to burn an effigy of the chief minister, M. Karunanidhi, it said.

Sultan Pasha, who set himself alight on Saturday, died in a government hospital in the southern city of Madras, where Jayalalitha spent her first night in jail after being arrested in a corruption case, United News of India (UNI) said.

Jayalalitha, a former film star, was charged on Saturday with ordering some 85 million rupees ($2.4 million) worth of excess spending on 45,302 television sets for villagers while she was Tamil Nadu's chief minister. She denied any wrongdoing.
Since her party was trounced in the state elections, Jayalalitha, 48, has been charged in seven corruption cases ranging from foreign exchange to income tax violations.
Four teams of officials continued on Sunday to search her Madras residence, UNI said. A jeweller was brought in to weigh seized jewellery, it said.
Jayalalitha spent her first night in Madras central jail sleeping on a bedsheet on the floor, news agencies said.
UNI said she was given rice gruel in an aluminium bowl for breakfast.

The state government, wary of critics who said Jayalalitha had been victimised, said she had since been granted special facilities and given a fan, a cot, magazines, newspapers, mineral water to drink and hot water for her bath.
